title: Finite representable pullbacks of a formal quotient chart
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], $\mathcal X$ a locally Noetherian Deligne--Mumford stack over $\Omega$, and $x\in\mathcal X(\Omega)$. Use stacks and 2-fibre products as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Write $\mathcal G_x$ for the residual gerbe, the full substack of objects locally isomorphic to $x$. Let $H$ be a finite group and $(R,\mathfrak m)$ a complete Noetherian local $\Omega$-algebra with residue field $\Omega$ and a continuous $\Omega$-linear action of $H$. Suppose $f:\operatorname{Spec}R\to\mathcal X$ restricts on the closed point to $x$ and induces a specified equivalence $\widehat{\mathcal X}_{\mathcal G_x}\simeq[\operatorname{Spf}R/H]$ under which its formal restriction is the canonical atlas. For every morphism of stacks $p:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal X$ representable by finite schemes, meaning that for every scheme $T\to\mathcal X$ its 2-pullback is a scheme finite over $T$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], put $\operatorname{Spec}C=\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal X}\operatorname{Spec}R$. Then $C$ is a finite $R$-algebra, complete for $\mathfrak m C$, and the descent arrows on the formal chart induce a continuous semilinear $H$-action on $C$ extending that on $R$. There is a canonical equivalence over $[\operatorname{Spf}R/H]$,
$$\widehat{\mathcal Y}_{p^{-1}\mathcal G_x}\simeq[\operatorname{Spf}C/H].$$
Formal completion along a closed substack means the compatible system of its infinitesimal neighbourhoods, and $\operatorname{Spf}C$ uses $\operatorname{Spec}(C/\mathfrak m^n C)$. Quotients mean groupoids of $H$-torsors with equivariant maps. No normality, dense open or normalization hypothesis is imposed on $\mathcal Y$. Noetherian, completion and finite algebra use [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Affine spectra and their contravariant maps use [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Tags 04M9 (lemma-quotient-stack-2-cartesian) and 044W (lemma-quotient-stack-isom), applied to each infinitesimal neighbourhood; algebra.tex Tags 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor), 07N9 (lemma-completion-finite-extension). proof.text: Apply the scheme-test definition of $p$ to $\operatorname{Spec}R$. Its pullback is an affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}C$ finite over $\operatorname{Spec}R$, so $C$ is a finite $R$-module by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian] with $J=\mathfrak m$ and $N=C$: $R$ is Noetherian and $\mathfrak m$-adically complete by hypothesis. Thus the canonical map $C\to\varprojlim_{n\geq1}C/\mathfrak m^nC$ is bijective. It is a ring homomorphism because operations on the limit are componentwise; consequently it is a ring isomorphism.

Write $R_n=R/\mathfrak m^n$, $C_n=C/\mathfrak m^nC$, $U_n=\operatorname{Spec}R_n$, and let $\mathcal X_n$ be the $n$th neighbourhood of the gerbe. The specified formal chart identifies $\mathcal X_n$ with $[U_n/H]$ and its atlas with the restriction of $f$. Put $\mathcal Y_n=\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal X_n$. Associating the triples in a 2-fibre product gives
$$\mathcal Y_n\times_{\mathcal X_n}U_n\simeq\mathcal Y\times_{\mathcal X}U_n\simeq\operatorname{Spec}C_n=:V_n.$$
For the last identification, a homomorphism $C\to A$ whose restricted map $R\to A$ kills $\mathfrak m^n$ factors uniquely through $C_n$; this proves the affine pullback assertion directly. All these identifications commute with reduction from $n+1$ to $n$.

source.place: Tag 04M9 (lemma-quotient-stack-2-cartesian), applied to the specified chart; affine quotient universal property.

proof.text: For a test scheme $T$, represent a point of $V_n$ by $(u,y,\beta)$, with $u:T\to U_n$, $y\in\mathcal Y_n(T)$ and $\beta:p(y)\simeq a_n(u)$. An arrow from $u$ to $hu$ in $[U_n/H]$ is the corresponding equivariant isomorphism of trivial torsors; its composites are given by multiplication in $H$. Compose $\beta$ with that arrow, leaving $y$ fixed. This defines an automorphism $\widetilde h_n$ of $V_n$ covering $h$ on $U_n$. Although triples are taken up to isomorphism, $V_n$ is a scheme, so natural isomorphisms give equal maps on its represented sheaf. Hence $\widetilde g_n\widetilde h_n=\widetilde{gh}_n$ and $\widetilde1_n=1$. These maps commute with reduction, since composition of the same arrows commutes with restriction.

source.place: Tag 04M9, action-groupoid case: compute arrows between trivial torsors.

proof.text:
Use contravariance of affine spectra to put $\rho_{h,n}=(\widetilde {h^{-1}}_n)^*:C_n\to C_n$. These are compatible ring automorphisms, satisfy $\rho_{gh,n}=\rho_{g,n}\rho_{h,n}$, and are semilinear for the given ring action on $R_n$ (the scheme action associated to a ring action uses inverse pullback). Via the canonical ring isomorphism of step 1 define
$$\rho_h((c_n)_n)=(\rho_{h,n}(c_n))_n.$$
The identities $\rho_{gh}=\rho_g\rho_h$, $\rho_1=1$ and $\rho_h(rc)=h(r)\rho_h(c)$ hold in every coordinate, hence in $C$. Each $\rho_h$ preserves $\mathfrak m^nC$: its quotient at level $n$ is $\rho_{h,n}$. It is therefore continuous for the $\mathfrak m C$-adic topology, as is its inverse $\rho_{h^{-1}}$. This is the required continuous semilinear action extending the action on $R$.

source.place: Tag 00MA, part (3), together with componentwise operations on the completion.

proof.text:
Check the presentation criterion [lem-sfb-action-groupoid-quotient-criterion] over $S=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ for $b:V_n\to\mathcal Y_n$, $(u,y,\beta)\mapsto y$. Every $y\in\mathcal Y_n(T)$ lifts etale locally to $V_n$: under $\mathcal X_n\simeq[U_n/H]$, $p(y)$ is an $H_T$-torsor $P\to T$ with an equivariant map $e:P\to U_n$, and $P$ is trivial on a jointly surjective etale family $T_i\to T$ (torsors as in [lem-sfb-action-groupoid-quotient-criterion]). The identity section of $P|_{T_i}\simeq H_{T_i}$ composed with $e$ gives $u_i:T_i\to U_n$ and $\beta_i:p(y)|_{T_i}\simeq a_n(u_i)$; then $(u_i,y|_{T_i},\beta_i)\in V_n(T_i)$ lifts $y|_{T_i}$. The structure isomorphisms are $\alpha_{h,v}=1_y$, since $\widetilde h_n$ leaves $y$ fixed; their cocycle identities are trivial. Its arrow space is
$$V_n\times_{\mathcal Y_n}V_n\simeq H_\Omega\times_\Omega V_n$$
on $T$-valued points. For $v=(u,y,\beta)$ and $v'=(u',y',\beta')$ an arrow over $\mathcal Y_n$ is $\gamma:y\simeq y'$; put $\alpha=\beta'p(\gamma)\beta^{-1}:a_n(u)\simeq a_n(u')$, so $\alpha\beta=\beta'p(\gamma)$. An equivariant isomorphism of the trivial left torsors is right translation by $h^{-1}$ for a unique locally constant $h:T\to H$, with $u'=hu$. The displayed equation then identifies $v'$ with $\widetilde h_n(v)$ via $\gamma$. Conversely $(h,v)$ gives $(v,\widetilde h_n(v),1_y)$. These constructions are inverse, functorial in $T$, and identify composition with multiplication, including when points have nontrivial stabilizers. The criterion gives the equivalence $F_n:[V_n/H]\to\mathcal Y_n$ whose atlas map is $b$ and whose arrows are the ones just computed.

source.place: Tags 04T4 and 04T5, action-groupoid criterion; examples-stacks.tex Tag 04WM.

proof.text: The equivalences in step 5 use exactly the object map $V_n\to\mathcal Y_n$ and the arrows computed in step 3. Restricting these maps to level $n$ from level $n+1$ gives those same maps at level $n$. The uniqueness clause of [lem-sfb-action-groupoid-quotient-criterion] supplies the compatible 2-isomorphisms of the equivalences; their cocycle holds by the same uniqueness. The level-$n$ identification of step 5 lies over $[U_n/H]\simeq\mathcal X_n$: on the atlas the two composites $V_n\to\mathcal X_n$ send $v=(u,y,\beta)$ to $p(y)$ and to $a_n(u)$, and $\beta$ is an isomorphism between them compatible with the arrows, because $\widetilde h_n$ composes $\beta$ with the arrow $u\to hu$ (the equation $\alpha\beta=\beta'p(\gamma)$ of step 5). Since every object of $[V_n/H]$ comes etale locally from $V_n$ and isomorphisms in $\mathcal X_n$ form etale sheaves [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], these $\beta$ glue uniquely to a 2-isomorphism of the two composites $[V_n/H]\to\mathcal X_n$; it is compatible with reduction in $n$ because the triple components $\beta$ restrict unchanged, so the 2-isomorphisms of the equivalences also respect the maps to $[U_n/H]$. The ideal defining $\mathcal Y_n$ is the extension to $\mathcal Y$ of the $n$th power of the gerbe ideal, which equals the $n$th power of its extended ideal: both are generated by products of $n$ local generators. Thus $(\mathcal Y_n)_n$ is precisely the completion along $p^{-1}\mathcal G_x$. On its atlas the ideals are $\mathfrak m^nC=(\mathfrak m C)^n$, so $(V_n)_n$ is $\operatorname{Spf}C$. Taking the compatible system gives the asserted canonical equivalence over $[\operatorname{Spf}R/H]$.
